title: Mila, Pipo, and the Night the Fireflies Went Dark
description: Mila, Pipo, and their friends search for the missing lights and discover how calm voices and company can help courage grow.

cover.alt: Mila and Pipo, at the lower left, look up at a night sky full of fireflies.

illustration.alt: Mila steps out of the house with an empty jar, and Pipo joins her in the garden at sunset.

blocks.title: Into the garden
lines: At six o'clock, Mila carries an empty jar out into the garden, with Pipo close behind.
They hope to watch the fireflies, but the orange sky is fading and the bushes are unusually quiet.
One light, two lights… where are the lights?

illustration.alt: The dark garden, Mila holding the jar, Pipo sniffing the ground, and Tito crying in four panels.

blocks.title: No lights
lines: The garden has turned unbelievably dark beneath the tree.
Leaves rustle, but no tiny yellow light answers them.

blocks.title: The empty jar
lines: Mila's jar catches the last bit of sunset.
She tips it toward a bush, but she can't find a single firefly.

blocks.title: A little trail
lines: Pipo puts his nose close to the damp ground.
A narrow trail leads between the roots; their adventure has begun.

blocks.title: Tito is crying
lines: Tito stumbles out of a bush with tears on his cheeks.
—They’ve all gone dark! —he cries, pointing up at the sky.

variants.correctFeedback: Yes, Tito came out with tears on his cheeks.
variants.retryFeedback: Look at the last picture on page two and find the tears.

variants.prompt: Who needed comfort when they met in the garden?

options.text: Tito, who was upset about the missing lights.
Mila, who had lost her jar.
Dora, who could not find her book.

variants.correctFeedback: Yes, Tito was worried, and his friends listened to him.
variants.retryFeedback: Return to page two and notice who comes out crying.

illustration.alt: Tito points to a cloud covering the moon; Mila and Pipo get ready to help him.

blocks.title: The cloud
lines: —A thick cloud covered the moon —Tito explains.
—The fireflies don't like the dark, so they hid their lights —he adds.

blocks.title: Together
lines: —I want to find them —says Mila.
—I'll come with you, even if I feel a little scared —Pipo replies.

illustration.alt: A snapped twig, Pipo in a puddle, an owl, frightened Tito, Pipo sneezing, and the stream.

blocks.title: The twig
lines: Crack!
A dry twig snaps under Mila's red shoe.

blocks.title: The puddle
lines: Splash!
Pipo lands in a puddle and sends water up to his ears.

blocks.title: The owl
lines: Whoo!
An owl calls from a branch, making all three friends stop.

blocks.title: Tito’s heartbeat
lines: Thump, thump!
Tito's heart sounds like a little drum in his chest.

blocks.title: The sneeze
lines: Achoo!
Pipo sneezes, rubs his nose, and takes another step.

blocks.title: The stream
lines: They reach the stream at last.
One light, two lights… where are the lights?

illustration.alt: The bark bridge over the stream; Tito crosses while Pipo and Mila wait for their turns.

blocks.title: The bark bridge
lines: Their old bark bridge is still resting on its two stones above the stream.
Mila checks the path across and reminds her friends to take turns.
Being courageous can mean taking one careful step, then waiting while a friend takes theirs.

blocks.title: The first turn
lines: Tito goes first, keeping his small paws close together.
He counts one when he reaches the far bank and turns to watch.

blocks.title: The next turns
lines: Pipo is second, with his tail held high.
Mila is third; she says three when her last foot leaves the bridge.

variants.correctFeedback: Yes, Tito took the first turn.
variants.retryFeedback: Look at the lower left picture on page five.

variants.prompt: In what order did they cross the bridge?
variants.correctFeedback: Exactly: they waited and crossed one at a time.
variants.retryFeedback: Reread the two lower pictures on page five and follow their turns.

illustration.alt: Mila, Pipo, and Tito visit the hollow tree; Dora holds her blue book with a yellow star.

blocks.title: Dora and her book
lines: At the top of the hill stands a hollow tree, the home of Dora the stork.
She comes down holding a blue book with a yellow star on its cover.
It's the book of lights, and she keeps it ready for anyone who needs a little help with the dark.

blocks.title: The riddle
lines: Before opening her book, Dora offers the friends a riddle.
—What has leaves but isn't a tree, and tells stories without a mouth? —she asks.
Mila listens to both clues while Pipo looks up at the leaves on the tree.

variants.correctFeedback: Yes, Dora looks after the book of lights.
variants.retryFeedback: Look at what Dora is holding on page six.

variants.prompt: What does Dora keep in the hollow tree on the hill?

options.text: A clear glass jar that she uses to carry water from the stream up to her home.
The book of lights, whose pages show how to help someone who feels frightened.
A box of dry leaves that she puts across the bridge whenever it starts to rain.

variants.correctFeedback: Yes, the book holds a way to help others feel less afraid.
variants.retryFeedback: Return to page six: find the star on the cover and reread what Dora brings.

illustration.alt: Lightning crosses the sky; Tito hides behind Mila beneath an empty comic burst shape.

blocks.title: Thunder
lines: Boom! Boom!

blocks.title: Staying close
lines: Tito ducks behind Mila as thunder rolls overhead.
She stays close, giving him time to feel steady on his feet again.

illustration.alt: Mila sits thinking, with a yellow light bulb above her head and a book beside her.

blocks.title: The song
lines: One light, two lights… where are the lights?

blocks.title: The clues
lines: Mila knows that leaves can grow on branches or be made of paper.
She remembers turning paper leaves at bedtime.

blocks.title: The answer
lines: —A book! —she says, putting the two clues together.

variants.correctFeedback: Yes, she thought about the paper leaves in a book.
variants.retryFeedback: Reread page eight and look for the two kinds of leaves.

variants.prompt: How did Mila work out the answer to the riddle?

options.text: She heard thunder and thought it came from a book cover.
She connected paper leaves with the stories inside a book.
She found a hidden firefly shining inside her empty jar.

variants.correctFeedback: Yes, she put the clues together to find an answer that fit.
variants.retryFeedback: Reread Mila’s thoughts on page eight: what has leaves and tells stories?

illustration.alt: An open book, Mila breathing, Dora counting one, two, and three on her fingers, and Mila singing.

blocks.title: The open book
lines: Dora opens the book so everyone can see its pictures.
They show breathing, counting, and singing very softly.

blocks.title: A deep breath
lines: —Let's take a slow, deep breath —Dora says kindly.
The friends breathe in through their noses, then gently let the air out.

blocks.title: One
lines: Dora lifts one finger and counts one.
Tito copies her small, calm gesture.

blocks.title: Two
lines: Dora lifts two fingers and counts two without hurrying.
Everyone waits for the next number together, giving their hearts a little time to settle.

blocks.title: Three
lines: Dora holds up three fingers to finish the count.
Pipo lets his wings relax, and Tito notices that his heart is beating more slowly.

blocks.title: A quiet song
lines: Mila begins a soft little song.
Pipo hums on and on and on, keeping his voice gentle enough for shy listeners.

illustration.alt: Three fireflies in separate columns, each glowing more brightly than the last.

blocks.title: The first light
lines: A firefly blinks on beside a leaf at the edge of the path.
It is the first to leave its hiding place.
The friends keep singing and give it plenty of room to explore.

blocks.title: The second light
lines: The second firefly switches on nearby, helping illuminate the path.
Mila watches the two bright dots without reaching for them.
Her open jar can catch their glow while they stay free.

blocks.title: The third light
lines: A third firefly shines with an extraordinary golden glow.
Now three small lights dance above the leaves.
Tito feels as if his smile might grow all the way to the tips of his ears.

variants.prompt: How did the first lights appear?
variants.correctFeedback: Yes, they came on one after another.
variants.retryFeedback: Follow the three columns on page ten from left to right.

variants.prompt: What best describes how the lights began to return?

options.text: One firefly came out, and then two more joined it.
All three went dark before the first appeared.
Every firefly in the garden lit up at the same instant.

variants.correctFeedback: Exactly: the light returned a little at a time.
variants.retryFeedback: Reread the three columns on page ten and follow the first, second, and third lights.

illustration.alt: Six lights in the dark sky; three more appear as the cloud drifts away and the friends watch.

blocks.title: Four, five, six
lines: Four, five, six: more bright dots join the first three.
One light, two lights… where are the lights?

blocks.title: Seven, eight, nine
lines: Seven, eight, nine: three more lights appear above the path.
The heavy cloud begins to drift away across the sky.

illustration.alt: The sky fills with fireflies as the cloud moves away; Tito laughs happily.

blocks.title: All the lights
lines: —The cloud is leaving —says Mila.
—Our song helped them feel brave —Pipo replies, watching the lights rise.

blocks.title: Tito’s laugh
lines: —And you helped me feel brave too —Tito adds.
He laughs with his friends, and the tears on his cheeks are gone.

variants.correctFeedback: Yes, the quiet song helped them feel less alone.
variants.retryFeedback: Remember the singing on page nine, then look at the lights on page twelve.

variants.prompt: Why did the fireflies feel ready to come out?

options.text: Tito banged on the tree to wake them up.
Mila shut them inside the jar.
Gentle voices and company helped them feel brave.

variants.correctFeedback: Yes, the friends helped by being calm and staying nearby.
variants.retryFeedback: Reread Pipo’s words on page twelve and remember the song.

illustration.alt: Pipo carries the glowing jar, the friends cross the bridge, and Mila looks up at the sky.

blocks.title: A jar of light
lines: Pipo carries the open jar, shining with reflected light.
The fireflies are free to come close or fly away.

blocks.title: Back across the bridge
lines: The friends cross the illuminated bark bridge again.
They can see the stones below and where to place their feet.

blocks.title: Helping is brave
lines: Mila thinks about the little steps that brought them here.
You can feel afraid and still help a friend try something hard.
That is a kind of bravery too, she decides as they head home.

illustration.alt: The house and garden beneath a night sky full of tiny yellow lights.

blocks.title: The lights at home
lines: Warm little lights dance all around the house and garden.
Mila puts the open jar down, glad that a light can stay with you without being shut inside a lid.
One light, two lights… there are the lights!

options.text: They helped each other feel brave

variants.correctFeedback: Yes, they stayed together and helped one another.
variants.retryFeedback: Think about how Tito felt at the start and how he feels at the end.

variants.prompt: What does this adventure show us about bravery?

options.text: Being brave means never feeling afraid.
Helping someone else find courage is a kind of bravery too.

variants.correctFeedback: Yes, we can feel afraid and still be there for a friend.
variants.retryFeedback: Reread Mila’s thought on page thirteen, then look at the ending on page fourteen.

courageous.definition: Ready to try even when afraid.

unbelievably.definition: So much that it is hard to believe.

illuminated.definition: Lit so that you can see it.

stork.definition: A large bird with a long beak and legs.

firefly.definition: A small insect that makes light.

riddle.definition: A question with clues to work out.

puddle.definition: A small pool of water on the ground.

softly.definition: In a quiet or gentle way.

brave.definition: Ready to try something that feels hard.

garden.definition: A place where plants are grown.

paper.definition: Thin material used for writing or books.

finger.definition: One of the long parts of a hand.

fingers.definition: The long parts of a hand.
